input.command: cd /testbed/src/objects; grep -n "copy\|material" Mesh.js Line.js Points.js Sprite.js | grep -n "copy\|material ="

cd /testbed/src/objects; for f in Mesh.js Line.js Points.js Sprite.js; do sed -i 's/^\t\tthis\.material = source\.material;$/\t\tthis.material = Array.isArray( source.material ) ? source.material.slice() : source.material;/' $f; done; git diff --stat; grep -rn "this.material = source.material" /testbed/src

content.text:
Cloning a mesh, line, points object or sprite now gives the clone its own copy of the materials array. The materials themselves are still shared, so the clone's array holds the same material objects. A single material that isn't in an array is passed along as before.

The fix is a one-line change in the `copy()` method of `Mesh.js`, `Line.js`, `Points.js` and `Sprite.js` in `src/objects/`. `clone()` goes through `copy()`, so it picks up the change. I didn't run any tests or add new ones.

Sprites don't normally use a materials array, so the change to `Sprite.js` is only for consistency and does nothing in normal use.
